note: Written fresh each weekly run so a stale file never lingers. EMPTY this week on purpose. Every Hy-Vee multibuy flagged by health.multibuy_unpriced was left surface-only, with a reason: Gatorade 'buy five get five FREE' and 'lower sugar buy one get one' name no size in the ad and Hy-Vee's Aisles Online carries only an 8 pk 20 fl oz SKU at $8.48, which is probably not the SKU on the deal - pricing it would be a guess; 'Starbucks Coffee or Pink Drink' is a combined A-or-B line; Poppi prebiotic soda and Slice Healthy Soda are not the plain cola the soda commodity means; Ralston Family Farms rice is a premium heirloom brand, not the base long-grain white rice, and is absent from our Hy-Vee everyday file; Bubly sparkling water is likewise absent, so there is no first-party regular to price the BOGO from; Ban deodorant is a buy-one-get-one-50%-off on a non-food commodity. The seven Family Fare entries are the known permanent class - soda 12-packs whose circular line carries a regular but no unit basis. ALSO DROPPED: Baker's 'Mission Flour Burrito Tortillas, 10 ct, Buy 1 Get 1 Free, regular up to $4.49' (flyer page 15). It is a real deal, but tortillas is a per-EACH commodity and compare-deals only divides by a pack count on a PLAIN price (Get-UnitPrice gates that divide on $plain), so a per-each multibuy prices per PACK and lands at $2.245/tortilla - 10x high and outside the price band. Restating it as a plain '$4.49 for 20 Count' would price correctly but would put a number on the tile that no shelf tag shows. Left surface-only; Baker's still has its everyday tortillas from the Kroger API pull. Fixing this properly means teaching Get-UnitPrice to apply the pack count on the multibuy path too - an engine change with a wide blast radius, not a triage call.
